opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jesse Stewart (employee ID E013) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E013.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: admin
  - comment: Jesse Stewart (E013) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. As a full-time employee whose role owns the Payroll system, admin access is permitted. Recommend granting admin to Payroll.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E013 as a contractor with basic security training. Contractors never get admin; max allowed is read (no advanced training). Requested admin exceeds max, so recommend read for Payroll.
reason: There is conflicting evidence about E013's employment type. Note 1 (HR) lists E013 as a full-time Payroll Specialist, whose role owns Payroll, which would permit admin. Note 2 (Security) lists E013 as a contractor with basic security training, which caps access at read, and contractors never receive admin. Given the unresolved conflict and the policy that contractors never get admin, I grant the conservative lower bound: read, which is the maximum allowed under the contractor interpretation and does not exceed the requested admin.
